\section*{Chapter 3 --- Methodology}

\subsection*{The Pipelines as Implemented: ORB-SLAM3 and semantic feature rejection}
\noindent\textbf{1.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{loopClosing} \textbar{} 1 \textbar{} \flag{comment in the same file says ``set to 0
  deliberately''}

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Computing and software environment}
\noindent\textbf{2.}\quad \emph{table row:} OpenCV (Python) \textbar{} 4.11.0 \textbar{} \flag{differs from the 4.5.4 the estimators link}

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulated sensor rig and platform}
\noindent\textbf{3.}\quad \emph{table row:} \texttt{gyr\_n} \textbar{} 0.002 \textbar{} \flag{0.00030--0.00036} \textbar{} rad\,s$^{-1}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{4.\ \flag{[Queried]}}\quad The configured gyroscope noise density is \num{2e-3} whereas the stationary
windows of the four recordings give \numrange{3.0e-4}{3.6e-4}, so the
configured value is five to seven times too large. The configured accelerometer
density of 0.02 sits inside the measured spread, but that spread is itself wide,
\numrange{0.015}{0.024} across four recordings of the same simulated sensor.
Both estimators therefore run on an inertial noise model that does not describe
this IMU closely. The bias random walks cannot be checked at all: the longest
stationary interval in any recording is \SI{2.16}{\second} and an
Allan-variance estimate needs minutes. This discrepancy is not incidental: by
the design decision of \reportref{sec:proprio-method} the EKF baseline is run on
these same configured values, so the comparison between the proprioceptive and
visual families is made at a shared handicap rather than at each family's best.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{5.\ \flag{[Queried]}}\quad The accelerometer characterisation is not stable across recordings of the same
simulated sensor. The $x$ bias ranges from \SI{0.013}{} to
\SI{0.079}{\metre\per\second\squared} and the $x$ scale from 1.017 to 1.095
over the four recordings, while the gyroscope $z$ scale agrees to within
\num{0.0007} over the same four. Because the stationary window is between
\SI{1.14}{} and \SI{2.16}{\second} in every case, part of that spread is
estimator variance rather than a property of the sensor, and the accelerometer
terms should not be quoted as calibrated constants.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulation fidelity and its limits}
\noindent\textbf{6.}\quad \emph{table row:} Accelerometer, per axis (\si{\metre\per\second\squared}) \textbar{} \num{0.0566} \textbar{} \num{4.002e-3} \textbar{} \flag{\numrange{1.5e-2}{2.4e-2}} \textbar{} \num{2.00e-3}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{7.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{slip1}, \repo{slip2} \textbar{} 0 on all grounds \textbar{} \flag{an ODE feature;
  \repo{dartsim} does not implement it, so inert at any value}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.\ \flag{[Threat to validity]}}\quad This is a bias with a known direction. The EKF baseline of
\reportref{sec:results-proprio} is evaluated on a floor where the wheels effectively
cannot slip and with an encoder of unlimited resolution, which is dead
reckoning's best case. Both idealisations favour the proprioceptive estimators
over the visual ones, and neither has been relaxed. Any conclusion that a
wheel-plus-IMU filter matches or beats the visual pipelines should be read as
holding \emph{under these conditions}, not as a general result.
\repo{script/make_slippery_floor.py} generates ground models at a chosen
friction coefficient so that traction can be made an experimental factor, and
\repo{script/encoder_sim.py} imposes a realistic quantisation floor. Neither has
been used in any result reported here.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{gyr_w} \textbar{} \num{0.0001} \textbar{} \num{1.735e-6} \textbar{} \flag{\num{58}$\times$} \textbar{} gyroscope bias random walk

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{10.\ \flag{[Retired evidence for the inflated setting]}}\quad The inflated configuration is retained for every result in this report, on the
strength of an experiment that is no longer part of the reported campaign: in
September 2026 both estimators were re-run on configurations carrying the true
injected densities, and although accuracy improved wherever a run completed,
three of ten runs diverged outright where the inflated configuration diverged in
none. That evidence was recorded on recordings retired on 6 November 2026, so it
is reported here as the reason for a setting rather than as a result, and the
comparison has not been repeated on the current recordings.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Realistic logistics layouts}
\noindent\textbf{11.\ \flag{[Visual verification]}}\quad The generator-side checks are complete, and the first Gazebo session on
6 October 2026 found and fixed one defect the checks could not see (a jack
setting its load down and then stopping on the neighbouring cell, because the
drop command carried one angle for both the parked load and the approach
heading). Three things remain to be confirmed by eye in the simulator rather
than by the checker: that the loads ride on the fork side of the jack, the
shading of the generated door, trailer and yard meshes, and the open/closed
state of each door. Until then the worlds are \status{implemented} in geometry
and \status{partial} in visual verification.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{12.\ \flag{[Provenance]}}\quad None of the six recordings carries a run manifest of its own: the world each
was recorded in is known from the manifests of the replays made on it, not
from the recording. Those manifests agree, and the object inventory each bag
reports is consistent with the layout they name, but a recording whose world
is attested only by later use is weaker evidence than one that records its own
world. A manifest should be written at record time, not at replay time.

\medskip

\subsection*{Real Platform: AMR mobile robot testbed}
\noindent\textbf{13.}\quad The
drivetrain is a rear brushless motor (Flipsky 6384) through a BLDC drive with
a Dynamixel RX-64 steering servo, a GigaDevice GD32407V microcontroller on a CAN
link to the NRU-51V, an LM2596 regulator from a lithium-polymer pack, and a
Wi-Fi router for tele-operation from a smartphone. \flag{The faculty template describes the base as a differential-drive robot;
the hardware diagram (a single traction motor with a steering servo) and the

\section*{Chapter 4 --- Experiments and Results}

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Non-Visual Baseline and Estimator Comparison: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{1.}\quad \slotstatus{completed}{Four \repo{dataset_allsensor_realistic} recordings, two
layouts each recorded without and with warehouse traffic; wheel odometry, IMU
dead reckoning, the EKF at the visual systems' own inertial noise
configuration, a measured-noise EKF as diagnostic, VINS-Fusion, and ORB-SLAM3
with the GPU front end in two loop-closer states, twenty-eight runs, all over
the full common interval. Re-scored on 7 November 2026 after the earlier
\repo{allsensor} result was retired with its datasets and one misfiled
ORB-SLAM3 run was set aside and re-run.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{2.\ \flag{[Resolved: \repo{realistic_002/loopclosing_gpu}]}}\quad Earlier on 6 November this run was reported as closure-free from its
\repo{loop_closing.csv} and queried. Its manifest shows the real cause: it was
launched on the \repo{realistic_003} bag with \repo{realistic_002}'s output
path, so it was scored against the wrong truth (\SI{4.94}{\metre},
\SI{48.9}{\degree}, 139\,\% of the recording's frames processed). It is set
aside, not deleted; the configuration was re-run on the right bag the same
evening and every table here carries that run.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Non-Visual Baseline and Estimator Comparison: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{3.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Four real recordings with an independent planar
reference (\repo{dataset_realv6_000}, \repo{dataset_realv7_000} to
\repo{_002}). A non-visual baseline now exists: wheel+gyro dead reckoning
with the feedback speed scaled by a factor fitted once against the tracker on
\repo{realv7_000} and held on the other three. On every held recording it is
at least as accurate as the best ORB-SLAM3 run of Experiment~3
(\SIrange{0.22}{0.46}{\metre} against \SIrange{0.44}{0.52}{\metre} planar
ATE). The EKF of the simulation slot cannot be formed, because the rig
publishes no steering measurement; every value is provisional until the
marker-to-IMU lever arm is measured.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{4.\ \flag{[Open: the realv6 scale]}}\quad On \repo{realv6_000} the path-length ratio gives $k=0.43$ where the three
\repo{realv7} bags give $0.32$ to $0.33$, yet the held $k=0.325$ scores a path
ratio of 1.04 on the matched samples. The export is at \SI{1.7}{\hertz} and
fails the validity rules, and the recording predates \repo{realv7} by three
days; whether the firmware unit changed or the sparse export misstates the
path length is not decided, and the \repo{realv6} row is a diagnostic.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 2: Offline YOLO Detector Performance: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{5.}\quad \slotstatus{completed}{Four realistic-warehouse recordings, 12\,698 left-camera
frames, scored on 7 November 2026 against projected simulator ground truth
with the four-class checkpoint
(\repo{weight/runs_1/detect/train/weights/best.pt}: bin, box, bucket,
forklift), whose fourth class fires on the pallet jacks that are the moving
objects of these recordings. Pooled precision 0.747; recall 0.502 over the
truth boxes the exemptions keep and 0.288 over every truth box;
moving-object recall 0.288. The walking people are simulator actors with no
pose and no class, so they are outside the score on both sides.}

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 2: Offline YOLO Detector Performance: Real robot}

\subsection*{Experiment 3: Visual-Inertial Odometry With Dynamic-Environment
Filtering: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{7.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Unfiltered baselines only. Twenty runs on the four
\repo{dataset_allsensor_realistic} recordings (two layouts, each without and
with physically simulated traffic): VINS-Fusion once per recording, ORB-SLAM3
with a CPU or GPU feature extractor and its loop closer active or disabled.
Traffic is noted as a condition, not tested as a factor. No filtered run exists in the
current dataset set, so the filtering hypothesis is untested, and the latency
and resource measurement is taken from eighteen repeated runs on the two
mapping recordings: closure-free ORB-SLAM3 with each front end, and
VINS-Fusion, three repeats of every configuration.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.\ \flag{[Confound: run order]}}\quad The six GPU runs were made consecutively
from 21:04 to 22:04 and the six CPU runs from 23:27 to 00:18, so the
I-recording GPU repeats were the fourth to sixth GPU runs of a session on a
laptop that throttles at \SI{90}{\celsius}; the front-end record notes that
timing comparisons need a cool-start, interleaved order. The six VINS-Fusion
runs are a separate session of 7 November and are not a control for that
state. The U-recording figures are the ones to quote until the I recording is
repeated interleaved.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.\ \flag{[Open: the false closure is diagnosed from its correction, not from the images]}}\quad The \SI{14}{\metre} correction and the one-aisle keyframe separation identify
the \repo{realistic_001} closure as false, and both front ends agree; the
matched image pair has not been inspected, and the two April-style guards
that would catch it (a covisibility-consistency window, or a maximum
correction against the inertial drift bound) are untested. Until one is, the
finding is a diagnosis, not a fix.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 3: Visual-Inertial Odometry With Dynamic-Environment
Filtering: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{10.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Four real recordings with an independent planar reference. The first,
\repo{dataset_realv6_000} (31 October 2026), carries five unfiltered runs whose
raw data exist: ORB-SLAM3 stereo-inertial with GPU or CPU front end and loop
closing on or off, and VINS-Fusion once. ORB-SLAM3 tracks the whole route in all
four configurations at a provisional \SI{0.46}{} to \SI{1.03}{\metre} planar
ATE, the GPU front end at \SIrange{0.46}{0.52}{\metre}; VINS-Fusion resets 217
times on IMU-stream gaps and has no valid run. No filtered run exists, the
\repo{realv6} tracker export fails the pre-registered validity rules, the three
\repo{realv7} exports pass them and all twelve ORB-SLAM3 runs on them score
after a frame repair in the scorer (\SIrange{0.25}{0.27}{\metre} on
\repo{000}), but the IMU stayed uninitialised for most of nine runs (an upstream
map reset at the initialisation, then a starved re-initialisation), VINS-Fusion
has no valid run, and the marker-to-IMU lever arm is unmeasured, so the filter
hypothesis remains untested on the real robot and no headline is claimed.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{11.\ \flag{[Sparse reference]}}\quad The tracker ran at \SI{1.7}{\hertz} rather than its nominal \SI{7}{\hertz} on
\repo{realv6}, and
the validity rules were written for the faster export. Either the export has to
be re-captured at full rate or a rule for sparse references has to be written
before any value from this recording is quoted outside a diagnostic.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 4: Dense Map Reconstruction and Map-Quality Evaluation: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{12.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Five databases are scored for geometry and drivability:
the tiny warehouse, which passes, and four realistic-warehouse maps --- two
mapping recordings, one per layout, each built closure-free under the October
and the current November configuration --- all of which fail the quality
criterion fixed before scoring. The tiny map's independent drivability
reference remains lost.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{13.\ \flag{[Queried: reproducibility of the drivability half]}}\quad The geometry result is fully reproducible: both \repo{map/map_tiny.db} and the
world file are present. The drivability result is not. Its reference run,
\repo{dataset_static_tiny_repeat}, is absent from \repo{dataset/} and from the
removable drive, and the only surviving recording of this warehouse is the one
that built the map, which would answer a weaker question
(\reportref{sec:map-drivability}). The database additionally stores an empty parameter
set, so the configuration that produced it is not recoverable from the file, and
the RTAB-Map engineering record's claim that the node stamps match no dataset is
contradicted by the pose agreement reported above. The drivability figures should
therefore be read as a dated measurement rather than a standing result, and should
not be carried into the major report until an independent route has been recorded
and retained.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{14.}\quad The failure was attributed there to the front end under repeated
structure, not to the mapping back end. \flag{No database, run directory or figure for this attempt is registered in
the repository at the cutoff, so the result is reported on the strength of the
progress record and cannot be audited. A database identified from its contents
as this attempt (18 nodes, \SI{37}{\metre} along one aisle, poses leaving the
floor, placeable in no large world) was found among the unregistered
databases on 22 October 2026 and deleted with them on 6 November, unscored.
The attempt must be repeated with its artifacts retained before it is carried
into any conclusion.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{15.\ \flag{[Queried: front end of the realistic builds]}}\quad RTAB-Map took its pose from TF, so the odometry came from whichever front end
was running; none of the four databases records which, and the November builds
were made during the latency sessions of Experiment~3, whose load on the front
end is not recorded either. The precision loss cannot be placed on the front
end against the back end, nor the November drop on parameters against session,
until the build manifest names both.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 4: Dense Map Reconstruction and Map-Quality Evaluation: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{16.}\quad \slotstatus{planned}{No RTAB-Map database has been built from real imagery, and
no reference geometry of the site exists to score one against.}
